summary: Aermotor LX-24 fire tower burned 1967; 67-ft steel tower replaced it 1968; staffed to 2010, then standby; NHLR US 1109 (2015); cabin rental planned in 2020.

facts.design: 67-foot steel tower with 14 by 14 foot CL100 series steel cab (erected 1968 to replace an Aermotor LX-24 that burned in 1967)
facts.status_note: On standby since 2010; the 2020 report's cabin rental plan is the latest found, and no current rental listing was found

events.note: May 1924 newspaper: a sixty-foot steel fire tower being put up at the peak; the register dates the LX-24 to 1925
Aermotor LX-24 tower built (register and 2020 report)
Wind-whipped fire in the Danley Canyon area; lookout evacuated and said probably destroyed; FBI and Forest Service investigation
67-ft steel tower with CL100-series 14x14 cab erected to replace the LX-24
Registered August 30, 2015 as US 1109, NM 35; nominated by Mark Gutzman
2020 report: interior to be slightly modified for a cabin rental program; National Register addendum planned

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and the 2020 report date the LX-24 to 1925; a May 1924 newspaper describes a sixty-foot steel fire tower being put up at the peak. The sources do not say whether the 1924 work and the 1925 date refer to the same tower.

notes_for_editor: History is well sourced (register, 2020 report, 1967 newspapers). Present rental and access status is unverified: the 2020 report describes a planned cabin rental program, and two searches found no listing for this lookout. The Weed and Wofford results are other towers and were not used. The brief's access 'public' is unsupported; see corrections.
